hints: Look first at the left side of the spectrum around 3200 to 3600 cm-1, that broad deep dip tells you a lot about which functional group must be present.
Check for what is missing around 1700 to 1750 cm-1, a strong carbonyl absorption should appear there if a ketone or acid were present.
Notice the sharp dip near 1640 cm-1 combined with the alcohol O-H, and ask which alcohol option also contains that extra multiple bond.
walkthrough:
**Read the big broad absorption**

Look at 3200 to 3600 cm-1. There is a very broad, strong absorption with low transmittance.

That is classic for an $\text{O-H}$ stretch in an alcohol. It rules out any molecule with no O-H.

**Check for carbonyl C=O**

A ketone or carboxylic acid needs a very strong, sharp $\text{C=O}$ stretch at about 1700 to 1750 cm-1.

The spectrum has high transmittance there, then a sharp peak at about 1640 cm-1. That is too low for $\text{C=O}$ but perfect for $\text{C=C}$ stretch.

**Use the molecular formula**

Z is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$, so it has one degree of unsaturation.

$$ \text{Degree of unsaturation} = 4 - \frac{8}{2} + 1 = 1 $$
One ring or one double bond must be present.

**Match to the structures**

We need an alcohol (for the broad O-H) plus one C=C or one ring (for the formula).

Only but-3-en-1-ol, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has both an alcohol O-H and an alkene $\text{C=C}$ to explain the 1640 cm-1 peak.

options.A: Butan-2-one is a ketone. It should show a strong $\text{C=O}$ at about 1715 cm-1 and should show no broad $\text{O-H}$ at 3300 cm-1. The spectrum shows the opposite, a broad O-H and no carbonyl, so A is out.
options.B: Cyclobutanol is an alcohol, so it fits the broad O-H and the formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$. However it is saturated apart from the ring, so it has no $\text{C=C}$ to give the sharp absorption near 1640 cm-1. This is a tempting trap if you stop at O-H only.
options.C: Butanoic acid is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, not $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$, so the formula already fails. Its spectrum would also show a very broad $\text{O-H}$ from 2500 to 3300 cm-1 and a strong $\text{C=O}$ near 1710 cm-1, neither of which matches well here.
options.D: But-3-en-1-ol is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ with an alcohol and one $\text{C=C}$. The broad absorption at 3200 to 3600 cm-1 is the alcohol $\text{O-H}$, and the sharp dip near 1640 cm-1 is the $\text{C=C}$ stretch. This fits formula and spectrum perfectly.
